chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The milk of the cow is a medicine, and its butter is a healing, and its meat is an ailment.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the hadith describing cow milk, butter, and meat in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the medicinal hierarchy of bovine products, distinguishing between the general curative properties of milk, the specific healing efficacy of butter, and the potential pathogenic nature of meat. This teaching reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of *al-tibb al-nabawi* (Prophetic medicine), emphasizing that while animal products are permissible, their consumption should be moderated according to their inherent health impacts. The distinction underscores a holistic view of diet where moderation and selection are key to maintaining physical and spiritual well-being.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ismail Bin Abu Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The milk of the cow is a medicine, and its butter is a healing, and its meat is an ailment’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ’Isma‘il ibn abu Ziyad who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Cow milk and ghee (or fat) are cures but their meat is illness.’”
